note:
Recorded from the hand-written pack in the commit that deleted it. Every expectation describes that pack, not the real DigitalOcean API; a probe run replaces cells with observed evidence and cites the cassette.

Every step carries recorded_as: the pack spelled its operations CreateDroplet and GetDomain and bound them to the URIs the document gives DropletsCreate and DomainsGet, so a recording under the pack's names could not be replayed against the bundle at all.

The recorded input uses the model's member names -- droplet_id, domain_name -- because that is what the bundle is replayed with; the pack read `id` and `name`, and the invocation that produced this file translated. An addressed id is a reference rather than a literal, because the service issues it, and it was stringified before reaching the pack: a path label arrives as text, which is all a URL can carry, and the pack asserts it to a string.

No step is superseded whole. What every excused member has in common is that it was synthesized in Go -- `_wrap` and `_list` were instructions to a branch of the REST/JSON codec, not members the pack answered -- or that the document declares a shape the pack did not have. Both are `declared` evidence outranking `authored`.

What is still gated: the name the caller gave round-trips, the status the service invents is `active`, a domain's name is lower-cased on the way in and again on the way out, its ttl is 1800, and across the whole run the thirteen faults and their precedence -- a missing name is unprocessable_entity before anything else is looked at, a duplicate domain is a conflict whatever case it is written in, an unknown or deleted id is not_found, and a name freed by a delete can be taken again.
